title: Upper Deck: launch questions
lede: For the new Upper Deck website. Answer in your own words, in any order, over as many sittings as you like. Each part sends itself to Nicholas a few seconds after you stop typing (watch for the green Sent line) and keeps a copy on your phone.

sections.title: Upper Deck Ltd
sections.lead: 14 questions. Under each one is what Nicholas found on the old website and in the catalogs.

qs.t: The $250 minimum: do you count it at the regular price, or after the quantity discount?
qs.w: Both old websites say "$250 minimum" on every page. Example: 18 of one item can be $270 at the regular price but $240 after its quantity discount. Which one counts toward the $250?
opts: The regular price, before any quantity discount
After the quantity discount
qs.note: Does the $250 minimum also apply to orders picked up at the showroom? Yes / no. Anything else to add.

qs.t: The $75 showroom minimum: keep it on the new website?
qs.w: The old website has a separate $75 minimum for customers who buy in the showroom, on top of the $250 minimum for web orders.
opts: Yes, keep the $75 showroom minimum
No, drop it

qs.t: Paying for a web order
qs.w: The old website says: "check, Visa, or MasterCard for full amount, plus postage with order unless other financial arrangements have been made." The new website is built to charge the card once, when the order ships, for the goods plus the real freight.
rows: When should the card be charged: when the order SHIPS (goods plus the real freight), or when the order is PLACED?
A brand-new customer with no card on file places a first order. What should happen?
Are there customers who pay on terms (net 30: they get a bill and pay within 30 days) instead of a card? Which ones?

qs.t: Five items: the quantity price is HIGHER than the single price. Which one is right?
qs.w: A quantity price should be lower, not higher. These five came over from the old website that way. For each line type SINGLE if the single price is right, QUANTITY if the quantity price is right, or type the right prices.
cols: Your answer: SINGLE, QUANTITY, or the right prices
rows: 4+ @ $13.75 (the 2026 garden catalog prints 4 @ $11.75, same as single)

qs.t: 23 items: one price only, or quantity discounts?
qs.w: Right now the new website shows ONE price for each of these 23 items, with no quantity discount. The old website had quantity discounts for them; they were taken off the new website in August while the prices were being checked. Five of the 23 are printed in the 2026 catalogs with quantity prices; the other 18 are not in any book.
opts: Use the same quantity prices the old website had
One price only, no quantity discount
I'll go item by item in the next question

qs.t: Item by item
qs.w: For each line type OLD to bring back the old website's quantity prices, BOOK for the catalog's prices (the lines that name a page), ONE for one price only, or type the prices yourself.
cols: Your answer: OLD, BOOK, ONE, or prices

showIf.equals: I'll go item by item in the next question

qs.t: Items with a minimum (Min. 4 and so on): after the minimum, any number, or only in steps?
qs.w: On the old website this is set item by item. Example: the Cardinal is Min. 4 and then goes in twos (4, 6, 8). X2060 is Min. 4 and then any number (4, 5, 6). The new website now copies each item's old-website rule exactly (34 items were set that way on September 8).
opts: Keep it: each item works the way it did on the old website (Nicholas recommends)
Every item: at least the minimum, then any number
Every item: only in multiples of the minimum (4, 8, 12)

qs.t: Who handles the web orders once the new website is live? (initials are fine, plus a backup)
qs.w: The old website sends orders to its orders@ inbox and claims to its customer-service inbox.
rows: Which inbox should the new website send orders to? (the same orders@ inbox as the old website, or another)
Who reads that inbox and types web orders into the office system? Who is the backup?
When the warehouse runs out of an item, who marks it out of stock on the website?
Who charges the card and adds the freight?
Who approves new customer applications, and who reviews claims?

qs.t: Web orders and the office system
qs.w: The tech guy is setting up the office system. Its maker sells an add-on that pulls web orders into it by itself (price by quote).
rows: On the OLD website, did orders go into the office system by themselves, or did someone type them in?
Should the new website feed orders into the office system by itself, or should someone type them in?

qs.t: Launch morning: the old website stops taking orders
qs.w: On launch day (planned for Monday September 14, 8 AM; Nicholas confirms the day) the old website stops taking orders and the new one takes over. For the first week a few orders may still land on the old website.
rows: Who turns ordering off on the old website that morning and tells the office? (you, or initials)
Who keeps the list of any orders that still come in on the old website that first week, so nothing ships twice?

qs.t: Hiding prices from people who aren't customers: good enough, or hide everything?
qs.w: Today, on the old website, anyone can see your wholesale prices without logging in. The new website makes people log in first. A person with computer know-how could still dig out the single prices; the quantity prices and the catalogs stay behind the login (Nicholas checks this before the launch). That is no worse than today. Hiding every price completely means rebuilding part of the website, and the launch moves back.
opts: Good enough: same as today, open on time (Nicholas recommends)
Hide every price, even if the launch moves back

qs.t: The office check before a web order is filled
qs.w: Nicholas suggests this rule. Before the office fills a web order, someone checks two things: (1) the customer is an approved wholesale account, and (2) the order shows that wholesale prices were applied (the order says so). If either is missing, call the buyer first and enter the order by hand. Note: customers who applied years ago but were never formally approved can already log in and see prices, by your July decision; this check is only about the orders they place.
rows: Who does that check, and who is the backup? (initials)

qs.t: Showroom pickup: ask the customer once, not twice (this answer is used for Moby Dick too)
qs.w: Today the customer is asked twice. In the cart: "How will you get this order?" Then again at checkout, a Ship / Pickup switch the website adds by itself. Keep only one.
opts: Keep our cart question, remove the checkout switch
Keep the checkout switch, remove our cart question

qs.t: Hours: the old website says two different things. Which is true?
qs.w: Old website footer: Mon–Fri 8 AM–3 PM. Old contact page: Mon–Thu 8–4, showroom by appointment 8:15–2:15. New website today: Mon–Thu 8–3. The old Moby Dick website says the same two things.
rows: Showroom hours, or by appointment only?
Same hours for Moby Dick? (SAME, or the difference)

sections.title: Round 2: follow-ups from your answers
sections.lead: Thank you. Your answers set most of the launch. These are what's left; short answers are fine.

qs.t: The four items you marked "fixed prices": L434, UAL128, UDXL201, UT906. What should the website show for each?
qs.w: "Fixed" didn't tell me the number. Type the single price and, if there is one, the quantity price (example: 27.50 / 4+ 26.50), or ONE if there should be no quantity price.

qs.t: You chose the old website's quantity prices for the 23 items. Four of those old quantity prices are HIGHER than the single price. Keep them anyway?
opts: Drop those four higher prices, keep the rest as the old website had them (Nicholas recommends)
Keep them exactly as the old website had them
I'll write the right prices below
qs.note: Prices for any of the four, if you want to write them

qs.t: UH526 Door Latch is printed "Min. 6, Pkg. 2". Can a customer order 7, or only 6, 8, 10?
opts: Only in twos (6, 8, 10), it comes packed in pairs
Any number from 6 up, same as the other Min. items

qs.t: The $75 showroom minimum: who gets it?
opts: Any approved customer who picks "pickup" at checkout
Only accounts we have marked as showroom customers

qs.t: A first-time customer with no card on file places an order. You said the order goes through and the office calls for the card. Correct, nothing held?
opts: Correct: order goes through, office calls, nothing is held
No: the website must hold money before we accept any order

qs.t: The card portal you mentioned (customers hand us a card that goes into your office system): do you already have one in mind, or should Nicholas find one?
Showroom orders in the office system: what exact Source and PO should a showroom pickup order carry?
The office check after a web order (approved account + wholesale prices applied): who owns it and who is the backup, if the website's own checks ever fail?
Which list is the truth for "approved wholesale customer"? The new website imported 5,379 accounts and 3,786 of them were only prospects on the old site.
qs.ph: The office system list, the old website's approved list, an Excel you keep, or "ask me"

qs.t: The net-30 customers (about 30): can you email Nicholas the Excel from the office system, for both stores?
opts: Yes, sending it
It's in the office system, Nicholas can pull it
Ask me

qs.t: Launch morning, one name each: who turns the old website off, and who owns the list of orders that still land on the old website that first week?
rows: Turns the old website off (one name)
